content.introduction: The Ludwig Institute for Shared Economic Prosperity (LISEP) was created in 2019 by Gene Ludwig and his wife, Dr. Carol Ludwig, with a mission to improve the economic well-being of middle- and lower-income Americans through research and education. LISEP focuses on fact-based economic and policy research, including new indicators for unemployment, earnings, and cost of living to provide a more transparent view of the economic situation of all Americans. The institute's headquarters is in Washington, DC, United States, and it operates as a nonprofit organization. In January 2026, LISEP reported that more than a quarter of the workforce is now considered “functionally unemployed,” marking the highest level since June 2021.

The mission of LISEP is to improve the economic well-being of middle- and lower-income Americans through research and education. LISEP's original economic research includes new indicators for unemployment, earnings, and cost of living. These metrics aim to provide policymakers and the public with a more transparent view of the economic situation of all Americans, [...] WASHINGTON, Aug. 13, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Prospects for workers seeking jobs paying above poverty wages worsened in July, particularly for Black and Hispanic earners, according to the latest report from the Ludwig Institute for Shared Economic Prosperity (LISEP).
